title: Effective open charts over etale base neighbourhoods give algebraic-space descent
statement:
Let $p:S'\to S$ be a flat quasi-compact surjection of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $Y/S'$ be separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]) with a descent datum $\alpha$ relative to $p$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Suppose there is a set-indexed open covering $Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with the following additional data for each $i$: a factorization $p=r_iq_i$ with $r_i:T_i\to S$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $q_i:S'\to T_i$ a flat quasi-compact surjection; stability of $U_i$ under the restriction of $\alpha$ to $S'\times_{T_i}S'$; a $T_i$-scheme $Z_i$; and an isomorphism $Z_i\times_{T_i}S'\simeq U_i$ inducing that restricted datum [def-pc-fibre-product]. Work in the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with the indicated scheme coproducts in the big site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then the functor
$$X(T)=\{y\in Y(T\times_SS'):\alpha(p_0^*y)=p_1^*y\}$$
on $S$-schemes, with restriction by pullback, is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. There is an isomorphism $X\times_SS'\simeq Y$ inducing $\alpha$. Each $Z_i$ gives a representable etale morphism $Z_i\to X$; collectively they give a surjective etale scheme atlas $\coprod_iZ_i\to X$. Over $T_i$ the corresponding map $Z_i\to X\times_ST_i$ is a representable open immersion whose pullback by $q_i$ is $U_i\hookrightarrow Y$. The conclusion requires the supplied effective open charts; it makes no assertion for a general fpqc datum without them.

source.place: Agent local-chart gluing criterion, using Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), Tag 02L3 (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), and Tag 02VN (lemma-descending-property-etale); the algebraic-space atlas criterion is bootstrap.tex Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap). A direct proof of the criterion, including the equalizer sheaf, descent of open subfunctors and the atlas, is in report.md. No general fpqc effectivity of algebraic spaces is used, and 02W5 is not invoked for the fpqc cover.

proof.text: Write $T'=T\times_SS'$ and $T''=T\times_SS'\times_SS'$. All maps to $Y$ below are over the specified map to $S'$. The singleton $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering: above each affine open $V\subset S$, quasi-compactness gives a finite affine open cover of $p^{-1}(V)$, and surjectivity says that their images cover $V$; flatness is the other condition in the definition. The same argument applies to every $q_i$. Base change preserves these fpqc coverings. We use the transport notation $\alpha_{s_0,s_1}$ on any test scheme with two maps $s_0,s_1$ to $S'$ over the same map to $S$. The cocycle says $\alpha_{s_1,s_2}\alpha_{s_0,s_1}=\alpha_{s_0,s_2}$. Invertibility gives $\alpha_{s,s}=1$ and $\alpha_{s_1,s_0}=\alpha_{s_0,s_1}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum); Tag 022D (topologies-lemma-fpqc); the singleton covering follows directly from the definition

proof.text: The displayed equalizer defining $X$ is an fpqc sheaf. Indeed, given a matching family $x_a\in X(T_a)$ for an fpqc cover $\{T_a\to T\}$, its maps $T_a\times_SS'\to Y$ glue uniquely to $y:T'\to Y$ by representable fpqc descent and base change of the covering. Their structure maps glue to the structure map of $T'$, so $y$ is over $S'$. The equation $\alpha_{p_0,p_1}(p_0^*y)=p_1^*y$ holds after the fpqc cover $\{T_a\times_SS'\times_SS'\to T''\}$, hence holds by the uniqueness part of representable descent. This produces the unique section of $X(T)$; restriction is precomposition and preserves the equation. Every fppf covering is fpqc, so $X$ is also a sheaf on the stated big fppf site.

For $s:T\to S'$, evaluate $x\in X(T)$ on the graph $(1_T,s):T\to T'$ to obtain $z:T\to Y$ over $s$. Conversely, for such $z$, put $s_0=s\operatorname{pr}_T$ and $s_1=\operatorname{pr}_{S'}$ on $T'$, and set $y=\alpha_{s_0,s_1}(z\operatorname{pr}_T)$. The cocycle gives the matching equation on $T''$. Evaluating on the graph returns $z$, since $\alpha_{s,s}=1$. For a matching $y$, pulling its equation back along $T'\to T''$, $(t,s')\mapsto(t,s(t),s')$, gives precisely this formula, so it returns $y$. These mutually inverse formulas commute with every map of tests. Thus $X\times_SS'\simeq h_Y$. For two lifts $s_0,s_1:T\to S'$, the two evaluations of the same matching section are related by $\alpha_{s_0,s_1}$; consequently the induced descent datum is exactly $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum), cocycle and diagonal identities; explicit equalizer calculation

proof.text: Put $V_i=Z_i\times_{T_i}S'\simeq U_i$. The given inclusion $U_i\to Y$ and step 3 define a section of $X(V_i)$. The two restrictions to $V_i\times_{Z_i}V_i$ agree: under step 3 their two maps to $Y$ are related by the restriction of $\alpha$, and the supplied effective isomorphism identifies this restriction with the canonical datum of $Z_i$. Since $V_i\to Z_i$ is the base change of the fpqc cover $q_i$, step 2 glues this section to $c_i\in X(Z_i)$. Restriction along maps into $Z_i$ gives a natural map $h_{Z_i}\to X$, and together with $Z_i\to T_i$ a map $d_i:h_{Z_i}\to X\times_Sh_{T_i}$. After base change by $S'\to T_i$, its source is $U_i$ and its target is $Y$ by step 3; the map is the given inclusion. The comparison of the two local sections used here follows from the stated compatibility of the effective isomorphism with the restricted datum, not from effectivity of a general fpqc scheme datum.

source.place: Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum); Tag 023Q, applied through the fpqc sheaf constructed in step 2

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T\to T_i$ and $a\in X(T)$. On $T_i'=T\times_{T_i}S'$, step 3 turns $a$ into a map $y:T_i'\to Y$. Let $W'=y^{-1}(U_i)$, an open subscheme by base change of open immersions. On $T_i'\times_TT_i'$ the two maps to $Y$ are related by $\alpha$, and the two maps to $S'$ have equal image in $T_i$. Stability of $U_i$ under this restricted datum therefore makes the two inverse-image opens of $W'$ equal. Apply descent of compatible opens to the fpqc covering $T_i'\to T$: there is a unique open $W\subseteq T$ with inverse image $W'$. This construction commutes with every $T_0\to T$: the inverse image of $W$ has the required inverse image on $T_0\times_{T_i}S'$, so uniqueness of open descent identifies it with the open constructed for $T_0$.

source.place: Tag 03N0 (lemma-open-fpqc-covering), compatible inverse images and uniqueness; Tag 01JY (schemes-lemma-base-change-immersion)

proof.text: The open $W$ in step 5 represents $h_T\times_{X\times_Sh_{T_i}}h_{Z_i}$. To check this, let $b:A\to T$ be any test. Over the fpqc cover $A'=A\times_{T_i}S'\to A$, step 4 identifies a lift to $Z_i$ agreeing with $a$ with a factorization of $y|_{A'}$ through $U_i$. Such a factorization exists exactly when $b|_{A'}$ lands in $W'$, and is unique because an open immersion is a monomorphism. By uniqueness of open descent this is equivalent to $b$ landing in $W$, and the open-factorization lemma gives the unique map $A\to W$. When it exists, the resulting local map $A'\to U_i\to Z_i$ has equal restrictions on $A'\times_AA'$: the restricted datum on $U_i$ is the canonical one from $Z_i$. Representable fpqc descent gives a unique $A\to Z_i$, over $T_i$. Its image under $d_i$ is $(a|_A,A\to T_i)$, since this equality holds on $A'$ and $X$ is an fpqc sheaf. Conversely any lift has the specified local factorization. This proves the natural representing bijection and shows $d_i$ is representable by open immersions, with the required pullback $U_i\hookrightarrow Y$.

Now fix any $S$-scheme $T$ and $a\in X(T)$, without a map to $T_i$. Put $B_i=T\times_ST_i$. Apply steps 5 and 6 to $B_i\to T_i$ and $a|_{B_i}$, obtaining an open $P_i\subseteq B_i$. The fibre-product identity gives $h_T\times_Xh_{Z_i}\simeq h_{P_i}$: a section on either side specifies a map to $T$ and a map to $Z_i$ with equal images in $X$, and the latter also specifies the required map to $T_i$. The projection $P_i\to T$ is the open inclusion $P_i\hookrightarrow B_i$ followed by the base change $B_i\to T$ of $r_i$. Open immersions are etale, etale maps are stable under base change, and their composites are etale. Hence every $h_{Z_i}\to X$ is representable etale, as asserted.

Let $Z=\coprod_iZ_i$ and let $c:h_Z\to X$ be the section whose restrictions are the $c_i$. It exists because the summand inclusions are open immersions, hence etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and they are jointly surjective; so they form an fppf covering of $Z$ with empty pairwise overlaps, and $X$ is an fppf sheaf by step 2. For the test $(T,a)$ of step 7 put $P=\coprod_iP_i$. A morphism $A\to Z$ specifies the inverse images $A_i$ of its summands, a disjoint clopen partition of $A$, and maps $A_i\to Z_i$. The equality of its image in $X(A)$ with $a|_A$ is equivalent, by the sheaf condition on this open cover, to the corresponding equalities on every $A_i$. Step 7 identifies these with maps $A_i\to P_i$ over $T$. Conversely such a partition and maps glue uniquely to $A\to P$, since the summands cover $P$. This gives $h_T\times_Xh_Z\simeq h_P$. Thus $c$ is representable. Its base change $P\to T$ is etale by locality on the source applied to its summands $P_i\to T$. All coproducts used are among those allowed in the statement.

source.place: Schemes, coproduct construction; Tag 02GJ (morphisms-lemma-etale-characterize); Tag 023Q supplies the Zariski sheaf condition as in step 2

proof.text: The base change $P\to T$ is surjective. Indeed $T'=T\times_SS'\to T$ is an fpqc cover. Under step 3 the pullback of $a$ is a map $y:T'\to Y$, and the opens $A_i=y^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $T'$. On $A_i$, the effective isomorphism supplies a map $A_i\to Z_i$ whose image in $X$ is $a|_{A_i}$ by step 4. Hence $A_i\to T$ factors through the representing scheme $P_i$ of step 7. For every point of $T$, choose a point above it in $T'$ and then an $A_i$ containing that point; its image in $P_i\subset P$ lies above the original point. This proves surjectivity of every scheme base change of $c$. The argument uses the covering of all of $Y$ by the supplied $U_i$, not a covering of $S$ by the images of the $T_i$.

source.place: Tag 03N0 (lemma-open-fpqc-covering), applied to the opens in steps 5-6; surjectivity checked on scheme tests

proof.text: The fppf sheaf $X$ of step 2 now has the scheme map $c:h_Z\to X$ whose every scheme base change is the surjective etale scheme map $P\to T$ of steps 8-9. An etale map is flat and locally of finite presentation by definition. Regard $h_Z$ and each $h_P$ as algebraic spaces via their representable sheaves. The fppf atlas bootstrap therefore applies and proves that $X$ is an algebraic space; its hypotheses do not require a pre-existing representable diagonal. The map $c$ is the required surjective etale scheme atlas. Step 7 gives the individual representable etale maps, step 6 gives their open maps over $T_i$, and step 3 gives the base-change isomorphism inducing $\alpha$. No additional effectivity theorem is used. If the index set is empty, the cover forces $Y$ empty, and the same construction has empty atlas and empty descended space.

source.place: bootstrap.tex Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), condition (4), through the existing condition-(3) node; spaces.tex Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space)
